package_info.why_malicious: No specific malicious package is analyzed in this report. The article discusses general supply chain attack scenarios (e.g., event-stream, Webmin, Browserify typosquatting, Mimemagic) and how SLSA and Sonatype products can help detect or prevent such attacks. No actual code or package is dissected for malicious content.

behavioral_signatures: Component in build does not match source repository or provenance
Dependency tree includes packages with mismatched or unverifiable provenance
Package name closely resembles a popular package (typosquatting)
Component is unavailable or removed unexpectedly from upstream repository
file_indicators: Package files with names similar to popular packages (e.g., browserify vs. browserfiy)
Build artifacts with provenance not matching expected source control
Unexpected or unverified uploader metadata in package repository
network_indicators: Download of packages from untrusted or unofficial mirrors
Build or CI/CD systems fetching dependencies from sources not matching official repositories
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor the provenance and source of all dependencies in the build process. Flag and quarantine any package whose source, uploader, or build provenance does not match the expected repository or source control. Detect typosquatting by comparing package names to popular packages. Use behavioral analysis to halt suspicious packages and subject them to manual review. Ensure all dependencies, including transitive ones, are verified and have a clear, trusted provenance.
